terms.plain_meaning: A rank-based test that checks if numbers consistently move up or down over time without assuming a straight line or normal distribution.
terms.technical_meaning: Non-parametric monotonic trend test evaluating rank concordance (S score) with variance adjustment for tied values.
terms.why_we_use_it: Resistant to outliers and non-normal atmospheric data distributions.

terms.plain_meaning: A robust estimate of how quickly a variable changes, calculated by finding the median of all pairwise slopes between data points.
terms.technical_meaning: Median of all slopes (y_j - y_i)/(t_j - t_i) across all pairs of observations.
terms.why_we_use_it: Can tolerate up to 29% gross data errors/outliers without breaking the trend estimate.

terms.plain_meaning: The number of genuinely independent observations after accounting for the fact that neighboring months influence each other.
terms.technical_meaning: n_eff = n * (1 - r₁) / (1 + r₁), accounting for first-order autoregressive persistence AR(1).
terms.why_we_use_it: Prevents false-positive significance in time series with persistence.

terms.plain_meaning: A corrected statistical test score that accounts for month-to-month correlation so you don't mistake natural persistence for a real trend.
terms.technical_meaning: Two-tailed Student's t p-value calculated using effective degrees of freedom (df_eff = n_eff - 2).
terms.why_we_use_it: Standard practice in climate science to prevent declaring random persistence as a genuine trend.

terms.plain_meaning: How much this month's weather is related to last month's weather (memory in the data).
terms.technical_meaning: Correlation coefficient between residuals at time t and t-1.
terms.why_we_use_it: High autocorrelation can make random noise look like a significant trend.

terms.plain_meaning: Values with the normal repeating 12-month calendar cycle subtracted out, leaving only the real underlying signal.
terms.technical_meaning: Difference between observation x_m,y and 20-year baseline mean for calendar month m.
terms.why_we_use_it: Without anomaly subtraction, winter smog peaks or monsoon rain peaks hide the true decadal direction of change.

terms.plain_meaning: A mathematical indicator that an observed pattern is very unlikely to have happened purely by random luck.
terms.technical_meaning: Test statistic exceeding critical threshold under the null hypothesis (typically p < 0.05, 95% confidence).
terms.why_we_use_it: Helps distinguish real environmental trends from natural year-to-year fluctuations.

terms.plain_meaning: A trend is visible, but complications like strong memory or non-linear curvature mean you should not assume it is a simple straight line.
terms.technical_meaning: Flags triggered by high autocorrelation (|r₁| ≥ 0.3), non-linear slope discrepancy (> 30%), or marginal adjusted p-values.
terms.why_we_use_it: Prevents overconfident or misleading claims about complex atmospheric dynamics.
